memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: They are to remove the ashes from the bronze altar and spread a purple cloth over it. Then they are to place on it all the utensils used for ministering at the altar, including the firepans, meat forks, shovels and sprinkling bowls. Over it they are to spread a covering of durable leather and put the poles in place. After Aaron and his sons have finished covering the holy furnishings and all the holy articles, and when the camp is ready to move, only then are the Kohathites to come and do the carrying. But they must not touch the holy things or they will die. The Kohathites are to carry those things that are in the tent of meeting. - Num 4:13-15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The altar, too, was prepared for the journey. But then comes a solemn warning: the Kohathites must not touch the holy things directly, or they would die. They could carry them, but only after the priests had covered them, and only by the poles — never with bare hands.

This is a sobering line, and we should not rush past it. It teaches, again, that God is holy, and that His holiness is not to be treated lightly. The Kohathites had a great privilege — carrying the very furnishings of God's dwelling — yet even they could not approach carelessly. Privilege did not remove the need for reverence; it deepened it.

We should let the seriousness of this sink in before we look for comfort. The holiness of God is real, and sin cannot casually approach Him. Left to ourselves, none of us could safely draw near.

But here is the good news the whole chapter is quietly pointing toward. What no Kohathite could dare to touch, we can now approach through Jesus. He, our great High Priest, has opened the way into God's presence by His own blood (Heb 10:19-20). The barrier that once meant death has been removed by His death for us.

So we come near today — not with bare, sinful hands, but clothed in Christ, welcomed and safe.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you take the holiness of God seriously?
- How does Jesus make it possible for you to draw near safely?
- What does it mean to come to God "clothed in Christ"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy God, I stand in awe of Your holiness. Thank You that through Jesus I can draw near to You, cleansed and welcomed. Amen.
